books.section: Topic 5.8 Military Conflict in the Civil War
Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

primary_sources: J. B. Elliott, Scott’s Great Snake (1861)

stimulus.source_note: J. B. Elliott, Scott’s Great Snake, entered according to Act of Congress in 1861 (Library of Congress, LOC 99447020). Public domain. Image from the shared pool.
stimulus.text: The cartoon map is titled “Scott’s Great Snake.” A giant snake coils around the Southern states, its head at the Mississippi River and its body wrapping the Atlantic and Gulf coasts. Small scenes fill the map: a train in Ohio, “Armed Neutrality” in Kentucky, and “Burning Massa Out” in Mississippi.

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: Which part of the plan shown in the cartoon would have taken the longest for the Union to achieve?

options.text: Winning a single battle in Virginia.
options.misconception: One battle is quick work; the snake shows a plan that takes years.

options.text: Blockading about 3,500 miles of Southern coastline.

options.misconception: Background: Lincoln was already elected in 1860, before the cartoon was drawn.

options.text: Moving the Confederate capital to Richmond.
options.misconception: Background: Richmond became the Confederate capital when Virginia seceded; it was not a Union task.

rationales.A: One battle is quick work; the snake shows a plan that takes years.
rationales.B: Background from the books: the South had about 3,500 miles of coastline, and closing it took years.
rationales.C: Background: Lincoln was already elected in 1860, before the cartoon was drawn.
rationales.D: Background: Richmond became the Confederate capital when Virginia seceded; it was not a Union task.
rationales.general:
1. The snake’s coil is slow work: it has to close every port along a huge coast.
2. Background from the books: the Confederacy had about 3,500 miles of coastline to guard and the Union had to cover.
3. A battle in Virginia takes a day; a blockade takes years to build.
4. The cartoon’s joke is that the snake squeezes slowly.
Remember: a plan that wraps a whole coast is a plan measured in years, not days.
